- If sentiment shows strong bullish (e.g., 1.00) in recent days, model tends to overestimate and overshoot — reduce forecast slope slightly.
- If sentiment shows strong bearish (e.g., -1.00) in recent days, model tends to underestimate — increase forecast slightly to avoid underreaction.
- After a sharp spike in price (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overcorrects — cap forecast rise to 5–7% max from peak.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.25), model often fails to capture mean reversion — adjust forecast to align with recent 5–7 day average.
- If true outcome shows strong divergence from model in first 5–7 days (e.g., >5% error), model is lagging — increase forecast early by 1–2% to catch momentum.
- If sentiment history includes multiple 0.00 entries, model tends to be overly conservative — add 0.5–1.0% upward bias to forecast.
- If model forecast is flat or rising very slowly while true outcome shows volatility, model is underestimating risk — increase forecast volatility by 1–2% in early days.
